runs.v: Building codes require flashing at roof-wall intersections and penetrations, per IRC Section R903.2, and a chimney requires step flashing and counter-flashing. Drip edge extends at least 2 inches onto the deck, fastened no more than 12 inches on center with at least 2-inch end laps, per IRC Section R905.2.8.5, and a kickout diverts water where a sloped eave meets a vertical sidewall, per IRC Section R903.2.1. A self-adhered ice-and-water shield runs under valley and penetration flashing, a membrane that self-seals around fasteners, per ASTM D1970.

sections.heading: Flashing Life Expectancy, the 25% Rule, and Roof Replacement

runs.v: What is the typical lifespan of roof flashing? Flashing is meant to last as long as the roof it serves, but rubber pipe boots often crack sooner, and a copper detail that has served West Orange winters for decades may still be sound. Asphalt shingles typically have a lifespan of 15-20 years, so many West Orange roofs need repair or replacement within that span; GAF and Owens Corning shingles offer manufacturer warranties of up to 50 years. Frequent inspections maintain roof integrity: check flashing visually every season and after severe weather.

Do roofers replace flashing? Yes, as a stand-alone repair or during a roof replacement, when worn step flashing, drip edge, and pipe boots are replaced rather than reused. Replacement is recommended for widespread damage or repeated leaks. What is the 25 rule in roofing? In New Jersey it is a permit threshold for buildings other than detached one- and two-family houses (see the permit answer below), and it is also a planning method: once damage covers more than about 25% of the roof, replacement usually beats another repair.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for roof flashing repair in West Orange?

runs.v: Not on a detached one- or two-family home. New Jersey's construction rules come from the New Jersey Uniform Construction Code, and under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 roof covering repair or replacement on those homes is ordinary maintenance. On a commercial, multi-family, or attached building, repairing more than 25% of the roof area within 12 months requires a permit, so confirm with the West Orange construction office before that work.

faqs.q: Does flashing work on a West Orange historic landmark need extra approval?

runs.v: It can. A locally designated landmark or a property in a historic district can need extra review, so confirm with the West Orange construction office before work begins. National Register listing alone places no federal restriction on a private owner, per the National Park Service.

faqs.q: How is step flashing installed correctly?

runs.v: Step flashing weaves one separate metal piece per shingle course against a sidewall or chimney, so each piece laps the course below and sheds water down the roof. A continuous strip is defective, per InterNACHI, and a separate counter flashing caps the step flashing at masonry, per NRCA guidance.

faqs.q: Should I upgrade to copper flashing on my West Orange estate or Tudor roof?

runs.v: Copper has the longest service life of common flashing metals and suits slate-roofed Tudors and estate homes; a properly installed copper roof serves over 100 years, per the Copper Development Association. On a cape or Colonial, aluminum or galvanized flashing lapped correctly costs less.

faqs.q: Does caulk fix a flashing leak permanently?

runs.v: No. Caulk is a temporary fix; sealant dries and cracks within a few years, while properly lapped metal sheds water on its own.
